newsitem.title: UK: Export data support's palm oil on European market.
newsitem.headline: Export data support's palm oil on European market.

text.p: Export data from two Malaysian cargo surveyors underpinned palm oil prices in Europe in Thursday, but failed to set the market alight.
Malaysian cargo surveyor Caleb Brett estimated July exports at 722,389 tonnes against it's June estimate of 634,753 while SGS pegged sales at 710,836 against 611,368 tonnes.
European traders said the figures were within expectations.
"The numbers are about what we expected, had they been lower with output rising it would have been very bearish for the market," said one.
"The market needs some healthy export figures now and palm oil seems to have been finding some new friends lately," said another.
Palm oil prices in Europe changed very little on Thursday following the data as traders had already built in a certain amount of protection against a rally in Malaysia during Wednesday afternoon.
In slow trading refined palm oil sellers were unchanged to $2.50 up after olein traded at $511 a tonne for Sep and $515 for Jan/Mar fob Malaysian ports.
Crude palm oil cif Europe was unchanged to $2.50 higher with no trade reported.
Lower Chicago futures and a slightly easing in the dollar against Europe currency lead to reduction of around 0.50 to one guilder in soft oil prices.
Lauric oils were quiet with coconut oil unchanged to $2.50 down while palmkernel oil was $5 lower.
